title: Locally Lipschitz construction of rapidly decreasing character models from generator brackets for concrete regularity structures satisfying assumptions A through C
source_title: Paracontrolled calculus and regularity structures II
author: Ismael Bailleul; Masato Hoshino
difficulty_reason: The standard reconstruction and paraproduct estimates do not construct all positive-sector character coordinates from arbitrary generator brackets. The author introduces an intermediate negative-homogeneity regularity structure and then proves the derivative and two-point character bounds by a two-scale dyadic Taylor-remainder induction. Those uniform rapidly decreasing estimates close the algebraic extension and local Lipschitz construction rather than assuming an existing model.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Theorem17 in the isotropic rapidly decreasing setting, exact finite generator/preorder/noninteger homogeneity requirements(A–C), polynomial character normalization and Definition10 model bounds. Full new auxiliary negative-homogeneity model, character identities, dyadic kernel estimates and induction read, including AppendixB weighted reconstruction and paraproduct decomposition. Standard Littlewood–Paley bounds, prior cited paracontrolled associator identities and Hairer reconstruction uniqueness are explicit existing research foundations. The proof allows any integer auxiliary m>|tau|; use its even-integer choices so |gradient|^m is a local differential operator preserving all rapid polynomial weights, without claiming the blanket odd-m mapping assertion on13. AppendixB gives the complete m=0 estimates and explicit annular kernels/scalings for the modified operators before saying the proof can be repeated; this is bounded kernel-weight verification rather than omitted new model-construction core. Individual m signs in displayedB.5 are reversed relative to the preceding supplied scalings; opposite factors cancel in the needed composite paraproduct bounds exactly as in53. No slowly growing AppendixC statement (details left to readers), anisotropic extension, density corollary or branched-rough-path parameter variant separately counted.
